To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fast-food consumption is high among New Zealand (NZ), especially among young adults.
fast-food consumption was more common among young adults, those of Māori descent, and urban dwellers.

(1) fast-food and restaurant/cafe food are consumed by a large percentage of New Zealand adults; (2) the consumption of fast food was more prevalent in young adults, Māori and those living in urban areas; (3) the consumption of restaurant food was more prevalent among higher educated adults, and (4) the most frequently consumed fast foods were bread based dishes, potatoes, and non-alcoholic beverage
In summary, our research is concerned with
the consumption of two types of foods that are not commonly reported in dietary surveys, but that have become increasingly important in the diets of many New Zealanders.
the characteristics of fast-food/takeway-food and restaurant/cafe food consumers among New Zealand adult population.
the consumption of fast food and the consumption of restaurant food.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consumption of fast food and/or restaurant food is not a healthy dietary choice.
fast food and restaurant/cafe food are important contributors of energy intake in the New Zealand diet.
the majority of fast-food consumers are not consuming fast food as their main meal, and the majority of fast food consumed is not contributing to the total energy intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fast-food/take-away food industry has been able to successfully market their products to the New Zealand population and that this is a major contributor of energy to our diets, particularly among young adults.

fast-food/take-away food and restaurant/cafe food are consumed by a significant proportion of the population and that these foods make a substantial contribution to the energy and nutrient intakes of the New Zealand population.
the fast-food industry in New Zealand is a major contributor to the dietary intake of New Zealand adults, especially among young adults and Māori.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a better understanding of the factors that influence fast-food and restaurant/cafe food consumption, and how this can be used to inform public health policy and practice.
there are significant differences in the consumption of fast food between different demographic groups.
fast food and restaurant foods are important components of the diet for a significant proportion of the NZ population, with a higher prevalence in young adults.
